fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 4 says, “Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.” Scattered, and still preaching the word wherever they went. When I got shoved into a junk drawer, all I did was gather dust.
I get why you'd pick it. Getting scattered feels like a reason to lie low. But Acts 8:4 says, “…preached the word wherever they went.” Preaching is what the verse gives us, not hiding.

Nope, friend. The verse says they preached the word wherever they went, and it doesn't say they returned anywhere. Peter and John are the ones who head back to Jerusalem later in this passage (Acts 8:25). Wherever these believers went, the preaching went with them.
Right on the money. Verse 5 says Philip, one of the scattered believers, “…proclaimed the Christ to them.” He went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ.
Nice try, baker, but no scrolls show up in this verse. Acts 8:6 says the crowds paid close attention to Philip's message and to the signs they saw him perform. Scrolls aren't mentioned.
Yes, joy! Verse 8 says, “So there was great joy in that city.” Unclean spirits came out of many, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed. I think that city had the best day it had ever had.
Not mourning, friend. Unclean spirits came out of many, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed. Then Acts 8:8 says, “So there was great joy in that city.” That's a day for joy.
Not prophecy, friend. Acts 8:9 says Simon, who was already in that city when Philip came, “…had practiced sorcery…” Prophecy isn't the word the verse uses. The Bible calls it sorcery, and so do I.

That's a great title, but it isn't the one in this passage. In Acts 8:10 the people say, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.” That's what they called Simon, and The Mighty Hunter isn't in that verse.

Right, it's False. Acts 8:11 says the people paid close attention to him because “…he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.” That's a long-running habit, not a brand new fan club. Simon had been the talk of the city long before Philip showed up.

I see where that came from, since scattering starts this passage. But in Acts 8:12, the people who believed Philip were baptized, both men and women. Scattered describes the believers back in verse 4. Here it's baptism.
Good church word, but it's not in this verse. Acts 8:12 says that when they believed Philip, “…they were baptized, both men and women.” Baptized is the word the verse uses.

Yes. Verse 13 says Simon “…followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.” This is the same Simon who had astounded people for a long time (Acts 8:11). Now the shoe is on the other foot, and I bet it felt strange.
Crowds are in the story, but they're not what the verse says astounded Simon. Acts 8:13 says he “…was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.” That's the answer here.
Yes, Peter, one of the apostles. Verse 14 says the apostles in Jerusalem “…sent Peter and John to them.” He's named right alongside John.
Right, John is the other name. Acts 8:14 says the apostles in Jerusalem sent Peter and John to Samaria. They're sent as a pair.
Andrew, Peter's brother (Matthew 10:2), is a fine name, but he isn't named in this verse. Acts 8:14 says the apostles sent Peter and John. Those are the two names it gives.
That's the prayer. Acts 8:15 says that on their arrival, Peter and John prayed “…for them to receive the Holy Spirit.” The Spirit is what that prayer was about.
Yep, money. Acts 8:18 says that when Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, “…he offered them money.” I think that's the moment the room got awkward.
Not punish, friend. Peter says, “Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.” (Acts 8:22). He had just told Simon to repent and pray to the Lord, and the next word is forgive.
Correct, it's True. Simon answers, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.” (Acts 8:24). He's asking for prayer after what Peter said to him. I think he's rattled.

It's actually True. Acts 8:24 says Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.” So he does ask for prayer. He even says why: so that nothing that was said may happen to him.
